words: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says reciting the opening verses of al-Kahf protects from the Dajjal; the author says this means reciting them with knowledge and understanding.
rows.anchor: من قرأ الآيات من أول سورة الكهف عصمه الله من فتنة الدحال يريد والله أعلم من قرأها بعلم ومعرفة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the earth will cast out its treasures, including gold and silver, and finally bring out the dead alive.
rows.anchor: تخرج الأرض أفلاذ كبدها ويحسر الفرات عن جبل من ذهب فى قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general wording about bringing hidden things forth confirms the report: the Quran focuses on the dead emerging alive, while the hadith focuses on treasures and minerals.
rows.anchor: فتوجه القرآن إلى الإخبار عن إخراجها الأموات أحياء وتوجه الحديث إلى الإخبار عن إخراجها كنوزها ومعادنها

words: حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The report that Arabia will again become meadows is linked to the earth’s flourishing before its sudden destruction; the author makes this a sign of the Hour and the world's near end.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى تعود أرض العرب مروجا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's fear that worldly abundance and adornment will be opened to the community is associated with the human tendency to transgress when self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فى مثل الدنيا إن مما أخاف عليكم ما يفتح عليكم من زهرة الدنيا وزينتها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Ramadan report about heaven's gates opening, hell's closing, and devils being chained is explained through fasting's acquisition of piety: it weakens Satan, closes paths to sin, and opens obedience.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا جاء رمضان فتحت أبواب الجنة وغلقت أبواب النار

words: واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت
واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When إذ follows اذكر, the command is to consider the remarkable events of that time; al-Zamakhshari also points this out in the Mary and Abraham passages.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به الامر بالنظر إلى ما اشتمل عليه ذلك الزمان لغرابة ما وقع فيه فهو جدير بان ينظر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In declarative speech, أو may express doubt, as in the ordinary example “Zayd or ʿAmr came.”
rows.anchor: الاول الشك نحو قام زيد أو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here أو signals ambiguity: the speaker knows the truth but leaves it unstated to the hearer.
rows.anchor: الثاني الابهام وهو إخفاء الامر على السامع مع العلم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “night or day” wording means the command arrives unexpectedly once the earth is adorned and its people feel secure; it does not imply doubt in God.
rows.anchor: يريد اذا اخذت الأرض زخرفها واخذ أهلها الامن اتاها امرنا وهم لايعلمون أي فجأة فهذا ابهام لان الشك محال على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni parses يزيدون as the predicate of an omitted subject, “or they increase”; أو can coordinate a nominal clause with a verbal clause because both are clauses.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن جني في المحتسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis supplies a pronoun referring to the hundred thousand: the people were sent to a hundred thousand together with an additional number.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قدروا في المبتدأ ضمير المائة الف والتقدير وأرسلناك إلى مائة الف معها زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, أو retains its ordinary sense of doubt, but the uncertainty is attributed to the addressee: an observer would judge them a hundred thousand or more.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل إن تكون على بابها للشك وهو بالنسبة إلى المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this comparison, أو marks variation: hearts sometimes become even harder and sometimes return to their former hardness.
rows.anchor: أي أن قلوبهم تارة تزداد قسوة وتارة ترد إلى قسوتها الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أو can specify separate speakers’ claims: Jews say only Jews enter Paradise, while Christians say only Christians; the same distinction explains “be Jews or Christians.”
rows.anchor: أي قالت اليهود لا يدخل الجنة إلا من كان هودا وقالت النصارى لن يدخل الجنة إلا الذين هم نصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing treats the lām as displaced before its phrase: it is an emphatic and oath particle that properly belongs at the start of the clause.
rows.anchor: فقيل هي مؤخرة والمعنى يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari answers that the lām is a non-governing emphatic particle, like emphatic من, so it may precede the relative phrase.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الزمخشري بأنها حرف لا يفيد غير التوكيد وليست بعاملة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi keeps the lām in place and reads من as an indefinite object of يدعو: the person invokes a deity whose harm is nearer than its benefit.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي اللام في

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad treats يدعو as a circumstantial clause and لمن as a new subject, but the author objects that this would fit a passive verb, not the active يدعو in the text.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد يدعو في موضع الحال والمعنى في ذلك

words: إِذًا لَّٱبْتَغَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِى ٱلْعَرْشِ سَبِيلًا
rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The completing lām occurs in responses introduced by إذن; al-Zamakhshari says إذن marks what follows as a response and consequence.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري إذن دالة على إن ما بعدها جواب وجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a response to لولا, the lām in لقد signals the conditional answer and emphasizes the threatened outcome.
rows.anchor: والموجهة في جواب لولا كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lām in a لو response can signal that the severe outcome is delayed, as in the adorned earth’s sudden destruction; omitting it can suggest immediate change, as with making water bitter.
rows.anchor: والمسبوقة في جواب لو كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath-signaling lām may enter a conditional particle after an oath stated or understood, marking the following answer as belonging to the oath rather than the condition.
rows.anchor: والمؤذنة الداخلة على أداة الشرط بعد تقدم القسم لفظا أو تقديرا

rows.speaker: النظام
rows.claim: Al-Nazzam holds that the Arabs could have matched the Quran, but God diverted them and stripped away their ability through an external impediment.
rows.anchor: وهو قول النظام ( 2 ) إن الله صرف العرب عن معارضته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge says humans and jinn cannot produce a like of the Quran even when united, which indicates their inability while their powers remain; otherwise the challenge would be pointless.
rows.anchor: فإنه يدل على عجزهم مع بقاء قدرتهم ولو سئلوا القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doctrine of diversion wrongly transfers the miracle from the Quran to God's removal of people's ability, despite consensus that the Quran itself is the enduring supreme miracle.
rows.anchor: هذا مع أن الإجماع منعقد على إضافة الإعجاز إلى القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If diversion ended with the challenge period, the Quran would cease to be miraculous; that contradicts the consensus that the Prophet's supreme miracle remains and that the Quran is his only enduring miracle.
rows.anchor: وأيضا يلزم من القول بالصرفة فساد آخر وهو زوال الإعجاز بزوال زمان التحدي

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr argues that if matching were possible but blocked by diversion, the speech would not itself be miraculous; the blocking would be the miracle, leaving no intrinsic superiority in the Quran.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر ( 2 ) ( ومما يبطل القول بالصرفة

rows.speaker: فريق منهم
rows.claim: One group claims everyone can produce a Quranic counterpart but lacks knowledge of its arrangement; if they learned that arrangement, they could reach it.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا بأعجب مما ذهب إليه فريق منهم أن الكل قادرون

rows.speaker: فريق منهم
rows.claim: Another group claims human and divine speech do not differ in this respect and that either can be inimitable on the same basis.
rows.anchor: ولا بأعجب من قول فريق منهم إنه لا فرق بين كلام البشر وكلام الله

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some allege that Ibn al-Muqaffa opposed the Quran, although what he wrote was only maxims.
rows.anchor: وزعم قوم أن ابن المقفع عارض القرآن وإنما وضع حكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author locates inimitability in the Quran's distinctive composition: its words are balanced in arrangement and meter, and its compound expressions reach the highest level of meaning and expression.
rows.anchor: الثاني أن وجه الإعجاز راجع إلى التأليف الخاص به لا مطلق التأليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Similes may join two sensory things, two rational things, or render an abstract meaning sensory; examples include the old date stalk, stone-like hearts, spiders, ash, and the donkey carrying scripture.
rows.anchor: ينقسم باعتبار طرفيه إلى أربعة أقسام لأنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey carrying books depicts people who bear the Torah by failing to live according to it; their burden is not physical carrying on their backs.
rows.anchor: لأن حملهم التوراة ليس كالحمل على العاتق إنما هو القيام بما فيها

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam bars comparing a sensory thing to an intellectual one because intellect is derived from sensation; making the derivative the original would reverse their order.
rows.anchor: أما عكسه فمنعه الإمام لأن العقل مستفاد من الحس

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other scholars allow the reverse comparison, illustrated by a poem likening stars amid dark to established Sunnahs among innovations.
rows.anchor: وأجازة غيره كقوله … وكأن النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unseen thing may be compared to a sensory impression by relying on familiar opposites: the heads of devils signify ugliness although people have not seen them.
rows.anchor: فشبه بما لا نشك أنه منكر قبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conversely, the imperceptible deeds of disbelievers are represented by the visible mirage; the comparison joins false expectation with severe need and deprivation.
rows.anchor: أخرج ما لا يحس وهو الإيمان إلى ما يحس وهو السراب

words: إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extraordinary is brought into familiar experience: the raised mountain resembles a canopy, while worldly life resembles rain-fed growth through its beauty, adornment, subsequent ruin, and lesson.
rows.anchor: والجامع البهجة والزينة ثم الهلاك وفيه العبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is not immediately known is conveyed through what is readily known: the Garden's breadth signifies vastness and makes its description enticing.
rows.anchor: إخراج ما لا يعرف بالبديهة إلى ما يعرف بها

rows.speaker: ابن الضائع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Da'i objects that the grammatical usage under discussion can properly apply to God; the author calls this a grave error.
rows.anchor: ورد عليه ابن الضائع بصحة وقوعها على الله عز وجل قال وهذا غاية الخطأ

words: لَوْ كَانَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ءَالِهَةًۭ مَّا وَرَدُوهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nonrational beings take pronouns and forms used for rational beings when they are represented as speaking or acting like humans; the author extends the explanation to the listed examples.
rows.anchor: لما أخبر عنها باخبار الآدميين جرى ضميرها على حد من يعقل وكذا البواقي

words: ولله يسجد ما في السماوات وما في الأرض من دابة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse includes nonrational creatures, the author says rational beings predominate in this construction; ما is used because the referent here comprises kinds of rational beings.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن ذلك ب ما لأنها واقعة على أجناس من يعقل خاصة

words: لِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا فِيهِنَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is preferred over من in “whatever is in them” because ما inherently covers all kinds, while من does not inherently include nonrational beings.
rows.anchor: لأن كلمة ما تتناول الأجناس كلها تناولا عاما بأصل الوضع

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki and al-Zamakhshari explain يذرؤكم as addressing humans and cattle together: it combines dominance of addressed over absent and rational over nonrational, instead of saying “you and them.”
rows.anchor: هكذا قرره السكاكي والزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ellipsis linguistically means removal; technically it is omitting part or all of a statement where evidence supports the omission. Calling omission without evidence اقتصار is imprecise because nothing is actually omitted.
rows.anchor: واصطلاحا إسقاط جزء الكلام أو كله لدليل وأما قول النحويين الحذف لغير دليل ويسمى اقتصارا فلا تحرير فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ellipsis differs from concision: ellipsis requires an estimated missing element, as “ask the town” means ask its people; concision uses few words that themselves convey many meanings.
rows.anchor: شرط الحذف والإيجاز أن يكون في الحذف ثم مقدر نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An implied element leaves a trace in the wording, unlike deletion; examples include an understood verb or construction in the cited passages.
rows.anchor: شرط المضمر بقاء أثر المقدر في اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The roots distinguish concealment from cutting away: إضمار hides an element, whereas حذف suggests removing and discarding it, which explains the grammatical contrast between overt and implicit forms.
rows.anchor: فإنه من أضمرت الشيء أخفيته

rows.speaker: ابن ميمون
rows.claim: Ibn Maymun rejects saying that a subject is deleted in the verbal-noun construction; he says it is implicit because the subject is an essential part of speech.
rows.anchor: ورد ابن ميمون قول النحاة إن الفاعل

rows.speaker: ابن جنى
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says an understood subject attached to a verb, as in قم, is implicit rather than deleted; he rejects al-Kisa'i's analysis in ضربني وضربت قومك.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جنى في خاطرياته من اتصال الفاعل بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes جاء, used when the arrival is visible or as if witnessed, from أتى for the unseen crops/earth; thus the earth's command comes as أتاها, while the visible command is جاء.
rows.anchor: وهم ممن يرى الاشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causative أجاءه means that something compelled or brought him along; it is not simply أتى, since the event lacks independence until it comes by itself.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد اتاه بمعنى ائت من الاتيان لان المعنى لا استقلال له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms of خَطَف distinguish habitual or characteristic snatching from an unusual, effortful act; the cited cases show habitual birds or demons, unusual human attack, and lightning's near-snatching of sight.
rows.anchor: فان الناس لاتخطف الناس إلا على تكلف

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib observes that أمداد is most often used for blessings, while مدّ is used for punishment, as in “We extend punishment for him.”
rows.anchor: قال الراغب اكثر ( 6 ) ما جاء الامداد في المحبوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عمل is narrower than فعل: every عمل is a فعل, but not every فعل is عمل; عمل involves duration or repetition, whereas فعل is more general.
rows.anchor: والفرق بينهما إن العمل اخص من الفعل كل عمل فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited ألا تعبدوا constructions, the verb can be subjunctive after an explicative أن, or jussive when the wording is read as a prohibition.
rows.anchor: أي بان لاتعبدوا فيكون منصوبا ويجوز جزمه لأنه نهى

words: فَتَزِلَّ قَدَمٌۢ بَعْدَ ثُبُوتِهَا وَتَذُوقُوا۟ ٱلسُّوٓءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the oath verse, وتذوقوا may coordinate with تتخذوا or with فتزل; its case therefore depends on which verb it follows.
rows.anchor: يجوز عطف وتذوقوا على تتخذوا أو فتزل قبل دخول الفاء فيكون مجزوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After قضى, ألا تعبدوا can be understood as بأن لا تعبدوا, or as a prohibition with a jussive verb.
rows.anchor: أي بألا تعبدوا أو على نهي

words: لِيَشْهَدُوا۟ مَنَٰفِعَ لَهُمْ وَيَذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām before ليشهدوا may be purposive or imperative; the distinction affects where a reciter may pause.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون لام كي أو لام الامر وفائدة هذا تظهر في جواز الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For readers who pronounce the lām with kasra in these verbs, it is the imperative lām.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم ليقضوا تفثهم وليوفوا نذورهم وليطوفوا ﴾ 8 فيمن كسر اللامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in ليكفروا and ليأكلوا is posed as an ambiguity between purpose and command, as in other listed examples.
rows.anchor: هل هي لام كي أو لام الامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited conjunctions support a subjunctive reading after a fāʾ or lām; in ألا تطغوا, the author allows either “lest you transgress” or a jussive prohibition.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ألا تطغوا في الميزان ﴾ 11 أي لئلا أو مجزوم

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh takes فيعتذرون within the preceding negation, since an excuse is speech; another analysis makes it an independent clause, with their speech counting as no speech because it misses its intended effect.
rows.anchor: داخل مع الاول في النفي عند سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في has spatial containment senses: both place and contained thing may be physical or conceptual, or one physical and one abstract; the first is literal and the fourth metaphor is closest to literal.
rows.anchor: للظرفية ثم تارة يكون الظرف والمظروف حسيين نحو زيد في الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في can mean مع, “with,” in the command to enter among God's servants.
rows.anchor: والرابع أقرب المجازات إلى الحقيقة وتجيء بمعنى مع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في can mean عند, “among/with us,” in Pharaoh's statement that Moses remained with them for years.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى عند نحو ﴿ ولبثت فينا من عمرك سنين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the women’s statement about Joseph, في carries a causal sense: “for this you blamed me.”
rows.anchor: وللتعليل ﴿ فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في can mean على, “on”: the wording about being in the ship is supported by a parallel verse that explicitly says “on the ship.”
rows.anchor: وبمعنى على كقوله تعالى ﴿

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats في as containment because a trunk is like a grave for the crucified; another says في suggests ease, since على implies upward movement.
rows.anchor: وقيل ظرفية لأن الجذع للمصلوب بمنزلة القبر للمقبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says في was chosen to suggest their crucifixion would be easy, since على suggests having to move upward.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنما آثر لفظة في للإشعار بسهولة صلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في may convey the meanings “to” or “into,” as in migrating in a land and putting hands to mouths.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى إلى نحو ﴿ فتهاجروا فيها ﴾

words: وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ فِى كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ شَهِيدًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في can mean من in the phrase about raising a witness from every community.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى من ﴿ ويوم نبعث في كل أمة شهيدا ﴾

words: فَمَا مَتَٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparative في stands between an earlier inferior item and a later superior one, as worldly enjoyment is only slight compared with the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وللمقايسة وهي الداخلة بين مفضول سابق وفاضل لاحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في may serve as an emphatic particle in the command to embark on Noah's ark.
rows.anchor: وللتوكيد كقوله تعالى ﴿ اركبوا فيها ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في may mean بعد, “after,” in the statement that weaning is after two years.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى بعد ﴿ وفصاله في عامين ﴾ 9 أي بعد عامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read في as عن in “blind in the afterlife”: those who disbelieved the worldly blessings described after “We have honored Adam's children” will be blind to afterlife bliss.
rows.anchor: أي عن النعيم الذي قلناه ووصفناه في الدنيا فهو في نعيم الآخرة أعمى إذ لم يصدق

words: إِنِّىٓ أُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ وَٱشْهَدُوٓا۟ أَنِّى بَرِىٓءٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud shifts from the statement “I call God to witness” to the command “you witness”: God's testimony affirms monotheism, while addressing the idolaters this way shows disregard for their religion.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن معنى إشهاد الله على البراءة صحيح في معنى يثبت التوحيد بخلاف إشهادهم

words: فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتَخْطَفُهُ ٱلطَّيْرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past-to-present shifts indicate ongoing or repeated action: disbelief is established, while obstruction continues at each moment; a past form would suggest that obstruction had ended.
rows.anchor: والحكمة في هذه أن الكفر لما كان من شأنه إذا حصل أن يستمر حكمه عبر عنه بالماضي

words: وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ ٱلْجِبَالَ وَتَرَى ٱلْأَرْضَ بَارِزَةًۭ وَحَشَرْنَٰهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past tense used for an unrealized future makes it feel certain and already accomplished; future tense for the past vividly stages the action for the listener. The past حشرناهم also underscores certainty after future verbs.
rows.anchor: والفائدة في الفعل الماضي إذا أخبر به عن المستقبل الذي لم يوجد أنه أبلغ وأعظم موقعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice of a verse ending can be inferred from its meaning: the named people are a subset of all worlds, which points to العالمين as the fitting cadence.
rows.anchor: فإن معنى اصطفاء المذكورين يعلم منه الفاصلة إذ المذكورون نوع من جنس العالمين

words: وَءَايَةٌۭ لَّهُمُ ٱلَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reader who knows this surah's paired-nūn endings can anticipate مظلمون from the verse’s sense: when daylight is stripped away, darkness follows.
rows.anchor: علم أن الفاصلة مظلمون فإن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “so they may see their deeds” signals the division that follows between those whose good and bad deeds are shown.
rows.anchor: فإن قوله ﴿ ليروا أعمالهم ﴾ يدل على التقسيم

words: أَفَحُكْمَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ حُكْمًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īghāl adds meaning after the sentence is complete: the judgment question is already complete, while لقوم يوقنون supplies a fitting cadence and adds that only people of certainty recognize God's superior judgment.
rows.anchor: فإن الكلام تم بقوله

words: وَلَا تَسْمَعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوْا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added مدبرين completes and intensifies the denial of hearing: deaf people may understand gestures, but turning completely away removes that possibility too.
rows.anchor: ثم أراد أن يعلم تمام الكلام بالفاصلة
